la:noun:voluntas.html:
vŏluntas, ātis, f.
1. volo
,
will, freewill, wish, choice, desire, inclination.
Lit.
In gen.: simul objecta species cujuspiam est, quod bonum videatur, ad id adipiscendum impellit ipsa natura: id cum constanter prudenterque fit, ejusmodi appetitionem Stoici βούλησιν appellant, nos appellamus voluntatem: eam illi putant in solo esse sapiente, quam sic definiunt: Voluntas est, quae quid cum ratione desiderat: quae autem adversus rationem incitata est vehementius, ea libido est vel cupiditas effrenata, quae in omnibus stultis invenitur,; : talis est quaeque res publica, qualis ejus aut natura aut voluntas, qui illam regit,: judicium voluntasque multitudinis,: mentem voluntatemque suscipere,: quid esset suae voluntatis ostendere,: has patitur poenas peccandi sola voluntas,: sit pro ratione voluntas,.—Plur.: ut ejus semper voluntatibus non modo cives assenserint, etc.,.—
Adverbial phrases.
Suā (alicujus) voluntate, or simply voluntate, of one's own will, of one's own accord, willingly, voluntarily (cf.: sponte, ultro),: ut verum esset, suā voluntate sapientem descendere, etc.,: suā voluntate, nullā vi coactus,: dictus filius tuos vostrā voluntate, : tu coactus es tuā voluntate,: istuc, quod expetis, meā voluntate concedam,: reditus in patriam voluntate omnium concedi videretur,.—Alone: nisi voluntate ibis, rapiam te domum,: quod jus vos cogit, id voluntate impetret,: aequius erat id voluntate fieri,: aliae civitates voluntate in ditionem venerunt,.—
Ad voluntatem, de, ex voluntate, according to the will, with the consent, at the desire of any one: ad voluntatem loqui,at the will of another,; : vultus et sermo ad aliorum sensum et voluntatem commutandus,: vix tamen sibi de meā voluntate concessum est,: illud accidit praeter optatum meum, sed valde ex voluntate,: ex Caesaris voluntate,; cf.: praeter legem et sui voluntatem patris studeat, etc.,.—
In partic.
Disposition towards a person or thing, good or bad: erratis, si senatum probare ea ... putatis, populum autem esse in aliā voluntate,: offensā in eum militum voluntate,: celans, quā voluntate esset in regem,: legati, qui de ejus voluntate explorarent,.—And with bona: neque bonae voluntatis ullum signum erga nos tyranni habemus,: quid nunc mihi prodest bona voluntas,; ; ; : non nudum cum bonā voluntate, sed cum facultatibus accedere ad patriae auxilium, Planc. ap. . —
More freq. voluntas alone = bona voluntas, good-will, favor, affection (syn. benignitas): voluntas erga Caesarem,; : summa in se (with summum studium),: mutua,: aliena a te,: voluntas vestra si ad poëtam accesserit,: singularis voluntas Campanae vicinitatis,: mansisset eadem voluntas in eorum posteris, etc.,. —
A last will, testament: defensio testamentorum ac voluntatis mortuorum,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; called also ultima,; cf.: per testamentum aut per aliam quamlibet ultimam voluntatem,other expression of his will,.—
An object, purpose: cum sint in dicendo variae voluntates,; cf.: quantam voluntatem habent ad hunc opprimendum, (14, 30).—
Transf. (acc. to 1. volo, I. E. 4. b.), of speech, meaning, sense, signification, import (only post-Aug.; esp. freq. in Quint.; syn. vis): verbis legum standum sit an voluntate,; so (opp. verba) ; ; cf.: quaestio juris omnis aut verborum proprietate aut voluntatis conjectura continetur,; : verborum vi aut voluntate,: legis,: nominis,.

la:noun:volumen.html:
vŏlūmen, ĭnis, n.
volvo; a thing that is rolled or wound up; hence
,
A roll of writing, a roll, book, volume (the predom. signif. of the word; cf.: codex, liber): volumen plenum querelae iniquissimae,: tuis oraculis Chrysippus totum volumen implevit,: volumen explicare,: caeleste Epicuri de regulā et judicio,: evolvere volumen,: hic plura persequi magnitudo voluminis prohibet, Nep. praef. § 8: illa uberius volumine amplecti,.— Plur.: evolvere volumina,: volumina ἀποφθεγμάτων, : pontificum libros, annosa volumina vatum, etc.,: signata volumina,; .—
In partic., like liber, of a separate portion of a work, a part, book: quoniam duobus superioribus (libris) de morte et de dolore dictum est, tertius dies disputationis hoc tertium volumen efficiet,: sedecim volumina epistularum ad Atticum missarum,; ; ; ; ; —
A roll, whirl, wreath, fold, eddy, etc. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): (anguis) sinuat immensa volumine terga,; cf. ; 11, 753; ; : crurum (equi),bendings, joints,: fumi,wreath, whirl,; : undae,: siderum,revolution,.—*
Trop., revolution, alteration, change: sortis humanae volumina,.

la:adj:voluptarius.html:
vŏluptārĭus (post-class. collat. form vŏluptŭārĭus, ; ; Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 92), a, um, adj.
voluptas
,
of or belonging

to pleasure or enjoyment, pleasant, agreeable, delightful; devoted to pleasure, sensual, voluptuous: quamquam Stoici communi nomine corporis et animi ἡδονὴν appellant, ego malo laetitiam appellare quasi gestientis animi elationem voluptariam, : res (with amoenae),: locus,: possessiones,: gustatus, qui est sensus ex omnibus maxime voluptarius,susceptible of enjoyment,: Epicurus, homo, ut scis, voluptarius,a man devoted to pleasure, a voluptuary,: homines,: quem mollem, quem voluptarium dicimus,; .—As subst.: voluptarii atque potatores maximi,; cf.: voluptaria, delicata, mollis disciplina,: disputationes,concerning sensual enjoyment,: secta,.—* Adv.: vŏluptārĭē, voluptuously: transactis paucis noctibus,.

la:noun:voluptas.html:
vŏluptas, ātis (
gen. plur. voluptatum and -tium), f.
Gr. ἔλπω, to hope; root ϝελπ-; cf. volo
, satisfaction, enjoyment, pleasure, delight (whether sensual or spiritual; syn. oblectamentum).
Lit.
In gen.: omne id, quo gaudemus, voluptas est, ut omne, quo offendimur, dolor,; cf.: huic verbo (voluptatis) omnes qui Latine sciunt, duas res subiciunt, laetitiam in animo, commotionem suavem jucunditatis in corpore, sq.: voluptas quae percipitur ex libidine et cupiditate (syn. jucunditas),: nulla capitalior pestis quam voluptas corporis,: ex tuis litteris cepi una cum omnibus incredibilem voluptatem,: nec vero sum inscius, esse utilitatem in historiā, non modo voluptatem. Quid? cum fictas fabulas ... cum voluptate legimus?: frui voluptatibus, et saep.: novum denique officium instituit a voluptatibus, an officer in the imperial household,master of the revels,—
Personified, Voluptas, as a deity, .—
Transf.
Of persons, as a term of endearment: mea voluptas,my joy, my charmer,: care puer, mea sera et sola voluptas,.—
Voluptates, sports, shows, spectacles, given to the people, : ne minimo quidem temporis voluptates intermissae,; ; ; Treb. Gall. 9 al. —
The desire for pleasure, bent, passion: suam voluptatem explere,; cf. ; cf. Gell. praef. § 14.—
The male semen, ; .

la:adj:voluntarius.gloss: voluntary, willing, of one’s own accord or free will, self-imposed
senses: voluntary, willing, of one’s own accord or free will, self-imposed
la:adj:voluntarius.html:
vŏluntārĭus, a, um, adj.
voluntas
,
willing, of his or its own free-will, voluntary.
Lit.
Adj.: milites,volunteers,; : ferocissimus quisque juvenum,: auxilia,: servi,: procurator,: est Asinius quidam, senator voluntarius, lectus ipse a se,.—
Subst.: vŏluntārĭi, ōrum, m. (milites), volunteers, ; ; ; ; ; and 512.—
Transf., of things: mors,suicide,: discessus voluntarius sine ullā spe reditus,: nam hoc ipsum ita justum est, quod recte fit, si est voluntarium,: verbera,: servitus,: deditio,: lex,: accusationes,: Junonis transitus in urbem nostram,: herba,growing of itself, spontaneous,.—Adv.: vŏ-luntārĭē, voluntarily, ; .

la:verb:voluto.gloss: to roll, turn, twist, or tumble about
senses: to roll, turn, twist, or tumble about
la:verb:voluto.html:
vŏlūto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a. and n.
id.
,
to roll, turn, twist, or tumble about.
Act.
Lit.
In gen.
With acc.: amphoras per terram,: pelagus (ventus),: pilas e fimo pedibus. i. e. to form by rolling together, ; cf. volvo, I.—With se: se in pulvere,to roll about, wallow,.—
More freq., mid.: ut gallinae possint in pulvere volutari,roll themselves, roll,: sus caenoso lacu,: super aureorum acervos ... toto corpore volutatus est,: volutati supra jacentia poma (irenacei),; cf. in allusion to the lit. signif. of the name Verres: quem (Verrem) in luto volutatum totius corporis vestigiis invenimus,: (animi) corporibus elapsi circum terram ipsam volutantur,: cum tibi pueri ad pedes volutarentur,; so in part.: genua amplexus genibusque volutans Haerebat,: (amnis) per cava saxa volutans,: in sacco et cinere volutantes,—
In partic., in mal. part., ; ; ; ; .—
Trop., to roll, roll about, roll along, etc.; to roll, wallow.
In gen.: vocem per ampla atria,to roll, spread,; so, vocem,: murmura,: confusa verba. .— Mid.: cum omnes in omni genere et scelerum et flagitiorum volutentur,wallow,: in omni dedecore,: inter mala plurima,.—
In partic.
To busy, occupy (of the mind): animum saepe tacitis cogitationibus,: in veteribus scriptis studiose et multum volutatum esse,; cf. .—
To turn over or revolve in the mind; to consider, weigh, ponder: rem in pectore,: gladios in comisationem praeparatos volutabam in animo,: haec secum volutantem in animo,: hoc eum jam pridem volutare in animo,: haec in animo voluta,; cf.: in pectore volutare,: ipse quid intra animum volutaverim ... omittam referre,: nihil umquam nisi sempiternum et divinum animo volutare,: aliud atque aliud consilium animo,; ; : aliquid mente,: tacitus mecum ipse voluto,: inter seque,: multa secum animo volutans,: haec secum volutans,; : secum corde,: suo cum corde,: aliquid in secreto cum amicis,to consider, discuss,: consilia de Romano bello,: quibus suā sponte volutantibus res inter se repugnantes obtorpuerant animi,.—
Neutr., to roll or tumble one's self (very rare): leone obvio suppliciter volutante,; so (cf. I. A. 1. b. fin. supra).
la:verb:voluto.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a. and n.

la:adj:volucer.html:
vŏlŭcer, ū^cris, ū^cre (
gen. plur. volucrium, Cic. ap. P.; masc. volucris, ; ; fem. volucer fama, Petr. poët. 123, 210; cf. acer; on the quantity of the u in volucris, v. ), adj.
cf. 2. volo
, flying, winged (class.; syn.: ales, volatilis).
Lit.
Adj.: bestiae,; : angues,: dracones,: Cupido,: natus,i. e. Cupid,: deus,i. e. Mercury,; cf. pes (Mercurii),; and: o nuntium volucrem!.—
Subst.: vŏlū^cris, is, f. (sc. avis, once masc., sc. ales: teneros volucres, Cic. poët. Div. 2, 30, 64),a bird, a flying creature,; ; ; ; : marinae, (4, 6), 11; ; : Junonis,i. e. the peacock,; cf. Junonia,; of the cock: volucres cecinere diem, Coripp. 1, 199; cf. ; the eagle,: obscenae,: Tityi volucres,vultures, (3, 13), 31; ; of the sirens,; ; ; : pictae,; : volucris parvula,the fly,.—
Transf., of any thing that moves rapidly, flying, winged, fleet, swift, rapid (mostly poet.; syn. velox): lumen,; cf.: ritu flammarum,: fumi,: aurae,; : nebulae,: procellae,: sagitta,; ; called also ferrum,: harundo,: equi,; ; : currus,: volucri freta classe pererrat,: jam volucrem sequor Te per gramina Martii Campi,speeding, running, et saep.—
Trop.
In gen., fleet, swift, rapid: nihil est tam volucre quam maledictum,: aliud genus (dicendi) est ... verbis volucre atque incitatum,: volucri spe et cogitatione rapiuntur a domo longius,: somnus,: fatum,.—
In partic., passing quickly by, fleeting, transient, transitory: o volucrem fortunam,: dies,; : fama,; : gaudium,.—Adv.: vŏlŭcrĭter, swiftly, rapidly (post-class.): congregati,: perurgebat nocentes innocentesque,.

la:adj:volubilis.gloss: turning, spinning, whirling, rolling, revolving (that turns itself around)
senses: turning, spinning, whirling, rolling, revolving (that turns itself around)
la:adj:volubilis.html:
vŏlūbĭlis, e, adj.
volvo
,
that is turned round or (more freq.) that turns itself round, turning, spinning, whirling, circling, rolling, revolving.
Lit.: buxum,i. e. a top,: caelum,: sol,: nexus (anguis),: volubilis et rotundus deus,: figurae aquae,: procursus,: aquae,; cf.: labitur (sc. amnis), et labetur in omne volubilis aevum,: aurum,i. e. the golden apple,; cf. : electrum,: pila,.—
Trop.
Of speech, rapid, fluent, voluble (the figure taken from rolling waters): vis volubilis orationis,: oratio,: rotunda volubilisque sententia,.—Transf., of the speaker: homo volubilis quādam praecipiti celeritate dicendi,; ; id. Fragm. ap. P.—
Of fate, changeable, mutable: vaga volubilisque fortuna,; cf.: cum videamus tot varietates tam volubili orbe circumagi,: fortunae volubiles casus,: volubilium casuum diritas,.—Adv.: vŏlūbĭ-lĭter.
Swiftly rolling, spinning, ; cf. .—
Trop., of speech, rapidly, fluently, volubly: funditur numerose et volubiliter oratio,.
